questions.feedbackIfWrong: A polynomial must have only whole-number exponents. $ h(x) $ satisfies this.
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a polynomial function?
hints: Check that all exponents are whole numbers.
Look for terms with variables in the denominator or under a radical.

questions.prompt: What is the degree of the polynomial $ f(x) = 7x^5 - 3x^2 + 2x $?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The highest exponent is 5, so the degree is 5.
hints: Look for the highest exponent of $ x $.
It is the power on the first term when written in standard form.
It comes after quadratic.
The word starts with 'c'.
questions.prompt: A polynomial function of degree 3 is called a ___ function.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Degree 3 polynomials are called cubic functions.

questions.prompt: The end behavior of a polynomial function is determined by:
hints: Think about what happens when $ x $ becomes very large.
Both the parity (even/odd) of the degree and the sign matter.
options: The degree and the sign of the leading coefficient
Only the leading coefficient, not the degree
questions.feedbackIfWrong: End behavior depends on both the degree (even/odd) and the sign of the leading coefficient.

questions.prompt: If a polynomial has odd degree and negative leading coefficient, the graph rises to the ___ (left or right).
questions.feedbackIfWrong: For odd degree with negative leading coefficient, the graph rises to the left.
hints: Odd degree, negative: $ f(x) \to +\infty $ as $ x \to -\infty $.
It goes up on the left side, down on the right.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: Even degree with negative leading coefficient means both ends fall (go to $ -\infty $).
hints: The degree is 4 (even) and the leading coefficient is negative.
Even degree + negative → both ends go down.
questions.prompt: Which end behavior is correct for $ f(x) = -2x^4 + 3x^2 - 5 $?
The graph of a polynomial function is always smooth and ___ (continuous or discontinuous).
hints: No breaks, holes, or jumps.
The opposite of discontinuous.

questions.prompt: For $ f(x) = x^3 - 4x $, what is the leading coefficient?
hints: Look at the coefficient of the term with the highest exponent.
The term $ x^3 $ has a coefficient of 1.
A polynomial of degree $ n $ can have at most $ n-1 $ turning points.
For 2 turning points, $ n-1 \ge 2 $ → $ n \ge 3 $.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The minimum degree is 3 because a cubic can have up to 2 turning points.
questions.prompt: A polynomial graph has two turning points. What is the minimum possible degree?

hints: Positive $ y $-values are above the axis.
The opposite of below.
questions.prompt: When $ f(x) > 0 $ on an interval, the graph lies ___ the $ x $-axis. (above or below)
questions.feedbackIfWrong: When $ f(x) > 0 $, the graph is above the $ x $-axis.

hints: The opposite of increasing.
The graph falls.
questions.prompt: A function is ___ when its graph goes down as $ x $ moves to the right. (increasing or decreasing)
questions.feedbackIfWrong: When the graph goes down to the right, the function is decreasing.
$ h(x) $ has an exponent of -1, so it is not a polynomial.
hints: Look for an exponent that is not a whole number.
Negative exponents mean the variable is in the denominator.
questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a polynomial function?
What is the constant term of $ f(x) = 4x^3 - 2x + 9 $?
hints: It is the term without any $ x $.
Look at the number standing alone.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: A negative average rate of change means the function decreases on average over the interval.
options: The function is increasing on that interval.
The function is constant on that interval.
The function is decreasing on average over that interval.
The function has a turning point in that interval.
hints: Average rate of change is the slope of the secant line.
Negative slope means the function generally goes down.
questions.prompt: If the average rate of change of a polynomial function over an interval is negative, what does that indicate?
Using a model to predict values far outside the original data range is called ___.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Predicting outside the data range is called extrapolation.
hints: It starts with 'extra'.
It can be unreliable.
